title: The residue translation functors on the sum of parabolic blocks
statement: Assume AC and finite classical $gl_n$ tableau blocks. Define $f_i$ by tensoring with its natural module and projecting onto the entry-multiset character with one $i$ replaced by $i+1$; define $e_i$ by the dual natural module and the reverse character change. On their direct sum these are exact and biadjoint, preserve projectives/injectives and commute with the restricted transpose duality. Equivalently $f_i$ is the generalized eigencomponent $i$ of tensor Casimir and $e_i$ is the generalized eigencomponent $-n-i$ on the dual tensor product. They are special residue translations, not automatically ordinary regular-wall translations. The Fock root label shifts by $\pm\alpha_i$; that label is not the classical gl_n highest weight.
strategy: General finite-tensor/block-projection biadjunction is the ACTUAL general clause of the published translation supplier, applied to V and V*, not a sequence of unproved regular wall crossings. Tensor finite modules preserves genuine parabolic local finiteness, and exact block projection/Levi Hom gives the same adjunction inside O^p. Restricted transpose duality fixes both finite natural modules with their respective forms, so each residue functor commutes with it. Highest-weight scalar Casimir calculation is supplied by the earlier local Casimir lemma before any head/socle consumer. All block labels are the explicit shifted-coordinate multisets.

references.title: Jonathan Brundan and Alexander Kleshchev, The degenerate analogue of Ariki's categorification theorem, Math. Z. 266 (2010) 877-919 (complete 44-page arXiv article)
references.locator: Section 3.1, display (3.6) and the preceding paragraph (printed pp. 19-21): $f_i,e_i$ defined by tensoring with the natural module and its dual and projecting onto a block, their exactness, biadjunction and commutation with duality; complete passage read.
